content.value_statement: Quetrex contributors need current project context before changing code. This skill organizes issue workflows, agent automation, quality gates, and reference documents for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Summarizes the Quetrex product, stack, automation flow, quality gates, and memory files.
Lists GitHub CLI commands for issues, pull requests, workflow runs, and logs.
Defines a structured issue format with acceptance criteria, context, tests, and priority.
Explains the AI agent workflow from issue creation through pull request review.
Points users to project status, checklist, architecture, roadmap, ADR, and contributing documents.
limitations: It is specific to the Quetrex repository and may not fit other projects.
It depends on GitHub CLI, repository access, and files that are not included in the skill.
It does not validate live project state unless commands are run in the repository.
Some dates or roadmap notes may need verification against current project files.

use_cases.title: Start a Focused Session
use_cases.description: Load Quetrex context, review pending work, and choose the next development path.

use_cases.title: Plan Agent-Ready Issues
use_cases.description: Convert feature ideas into clear issues with acceptance criteria, technical context, and test needs.

use_cases.title: Review AI Agent Output
use_cases.description: Inspect generated pull requests against quality gates, tests, architecture rules, and merge readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Start Quetrex Context
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Quetrex development workflow to summarize current project context, pending work, and the next safe development step.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Agent Issue
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me turn this feature request into a clear ai-feature issue with acceptance criteria, relevant files, tests, and priority.

prompt_templates.title: Review Agent Work
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the workflow to review a recent AI agent pull request. Focus on quality gates, tests, architecture fit, and merge readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Debug Automation Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze a failed Quetrex agent workflow run. Identify likely failure points, needed logs, quality gate failures, and corrective actions.

output_examples.input: Start a new Quetrex development session.
output: Review pending ai-feature issues and recent merged pull requests.
Check project status files and the checklist for current priorities.
Choose direct work or an agent-ready issue workflow.

output_examples.input: Prepare a feature request for agent automation.
output: Create a concise summary and measurable acceptance criteria.
List relevant files and project patterns to follow.
Define testing expectations and priority before applying the automation label.
Check tests, linting, build status, and coverage requirements.
Compare the implementation with the requested issue scope.
Confirm security constraints and human review before merge.

best_practices: Verify live issue, pull request, and workflow state before choosing work.
Use the issue template and acceptance criteria before starting agent automation.
Review tests, quality gates, and security constraints before merging agent output.
anti_patterns: Do not combine unrelated feature work into one agent issue.
Do not merge AI agent pull requests without human review.
Do not rely on the skill alone when project status files have changed.

faq.question: Is this skill general purpose?
faq.answer: No. It is built for Quetrex and assumes the repository structure described in the skill.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: No. It documents commands and workflows. The active AI tool or user decides what to execute.

faq.question: Which tools does it support?
faq.answer: It supports Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: What project areas does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers issue automation, pull request review, workflow debugging, memory files, status tracking, and quality gates.

faq.question: What permissions are needed?
faq.answer: GitHub CLI operations require repository access and any required workflow permissions.

faq.question: How current is the information?
faq.answer: The skill lists a last updated date of 2025-11-26, so users should verify live project status.
